topic: advocating for a daughter with endometriosis
voiceSample: My daughter has endometriosis, and her doctor says her only option is a full hysterectomy.
openingMessage: My daughter's doctor only offers hysterectomy
readyLine: I hear how serious this feels. I have options to walk through with you — my guidance is ready when you are.
suggestedQuestions: What should I tell my daughter?

sections.title: What I'm Hearing
sections.body: Your daughter has endometriosis, and her doctor has framed a full hysterectomy as the only option. I can understand why you're so concerned — that is a drastic recommendation for a young woman. I'm sorry she's in so much pain.

sections.title: The Hypothalamic Connection
sections.body: Endometriosis is very painful, but it isn't actually cured by hysterectomy. Endometrial cells can end up outside the uterus — possibly as early as fetal development — on tubes, ovaries, pelvic cavity, and rarely elsewhere. Estrogen and progesterone stimulate that tissue wherever it is. The body treats rogue cells as foreign; the immune attack creates scar tissue (adhesions), which often drives much of the pain. Medications that quiet the hypothalamus's GnRH signals for a few months can calm those pulses and help healing of that immune attack — her gynecologist can say whether a GnRH-based medication is right for her. You can read about these medications on drugs.com.

sections.title: What This May Mean
sections.body: There are options beyond hysterectomy. Laparoscopic surgery can clean up adhesions and endometrial cysts (blood-filled); not every microscopic cell can be found that way. Medical suppression and surgery are both conversations for her gynecologist — hysterectomy is not the only path.

sections.title: Questions for Her Gynecologist
bullets: Is laparoscopic cleanup of adhesions and cysts an option before hysterectomy?
Would a GnRH-based medication for a few months be appropriate?
What are the risks of hysterectomy at her age versus other approaches?

sections.title: Tests Worth Discussing
sections.body: Imaging and surgical planning belong with her specialist — bring the questions above to that visit.

sections.title: What You Can Do Now
bullets: Share this information with your daughter so she can advocate with you.
Ask the gynecologist specifically about laparoscopy and GnRH options — framed as discussion, not a demand to start a prescription without them.
Come back here when you're ready with more questions.

sections.title: A Word from Deborah
sections.body: Why don't you share this with your daughter and come back when you're ready? I'll be here for you and your daughter.

answer.closingLine: Prescription options are suggestions to discuss with her provider, always with a drugs.com reference. I'll be here for you both.
answer.summary: Daughter with endometriosis; hysterectomy framed as only option — other paths to discuss.

followUps.reply: GnRH-based medicines quiet hypothalamic pulses for a time and can help the immune attack on rogue endometrial tissue settle. Her gynecologist decides if that's right for her — read the medication pages on drugs.com together.
Hysterectomy does not cure endometriosis, because tissue can live outside the uterus. That's why other options deserve a full conversation.

fallbackReply: Bring that to her gynecologist, and come back anytime — I'm here for you both.
